info.name: Privilege MCP Client — K8s SE cluster (BFF relay)
info.description:
Tests the Privilege MCP client flow via the BFF relay deployed on the SE K8s cluster.

The BFF handles everything: it discovers auth from the mcpgw WWW-Authenticate header, registers a DCR client, runs PKCE against mcpgw's own OAuth AS, and relays MCP JSON-RPC. These requests are plain JSON over HTTPS — no bearer token of your own.

SETUP:
  1. The SE cluster stack must be deployed: see k8s/aws/deploy.sh or privilege/deploy-whole-stack.prompt.md
  2. No local cert setup needed — ai-demo.ping-devops.com has a valid LE cert
  3. Sign in to https://ai-demo.ping-devops.com in a browser first — the BFF reuses
     the existing PingOne session for prompt=none silent auth. Without a session, auth/start
     redirects through the PingOne login page (still works, not silent).
  4. Cookie sync: Postman must share the connect.sid cookie from ai-demo.ping-devops.com.
     Enable cookies for the domain in Postman's cookie manager, or sign in via Postman's browser.

FLOW:
  Run requests 0 → 1 → 2. After request 2, open authUrl in a browser (silent if already signed in).
  Then run 3 → 4 → 5. For OpenSearch: run 6 → 7 → 8 after registering cmuir-opensearch in console.

NODE: The K8s BFF (demo-api-server) reads PRIVILEGE_MCPGW_URL from the ping-mcpgw-secrets K8s secret.
  Request 1 overrides it for the current session only — restart demo-api-server to reset to env default.

variable.description: SE K8s cluster BFF (demo-api-server). Valid LE cert — no SSL exception needed.
SE K8s mcpgw — banking mcp-server backend (app: cmuir2)
SE K8s mcpgw — OpenSearch MCP backend (app: cmuir-opensearch). Register in Privilege console first.
PingOne application the BFF uses for Privilege SSO (env 01d89b06)

request.description:
Returns the current privilege MCP session state.

Key fields:
  oauth.authenticated  — true after a successful auth/start + callback
  config.mcpUrl        — which mcpgw the BFF is pointed at (from K8s secret or session override)
  mainAppAuthenticated — true when signed in to the SE cluster app
  tools                — non-empty after a successful tools/list

item.name: 2. Start Auth — get PingOne redirect URL

request.description:
Triggers the BFF to:
  1. GET mcpUrl — discovers WWW-Authenticate header from SE mcpgw
  2. DCR on mcpgw OAuth AS (registers a PKCE client at /mcpgw/cmuir2/register)
  3. Build the PingOne authorization URL (prompt=none if SE app session exists)
  4. Return { authUrl } for the browser to follow

AFTER: open authUrl in a browser where you are signed in to https://ai-demo.ping-devops.com.
Silent auth (prompt=none) completes instantly when a PingOne session exists.

IMPORTANT: If mcpgw was recently restarted, DCR client state is lost. The BFF will auto-register
a fresh client on the next auth/start — restart the BFF pod if you see 'Unknown client'.

exec: console.log('\n=== OPEN THIS URL IN A BROWSER ===');
console.log('Silent if signed in to ai-demo.ping-devops.com. Then run request 3.');

request.description:
Calls tools/list via the Privilege gateway.

Requires auth (complete the request 2 browser flow first). Privilege enforces its policy per tool.

Expect: { tools: [...] } — banking mcp-server tools via cmuir2.

Calls a specific tool through the Privilege gateway.

  200 + result data: policy grants access — Privilege PERMIT
  403:               Privilege DENY — this is the demo feature working
  401:               token expired — re-run request 2

Change 'name' to any tool from the tools/list response.
Send any raw MCP JSON-RPC. Change method/params as needed. The BFF handles token and session.

item.name: OpenSearch app (register cmuir-opensearch in console first)
6. Configure — switch to OpenSearch mcpgw URL

request.description:
Switches to the OpenSearch Privilege app for this session.

PREREQUISITE — register in Privilege console:
  AI Security > Agentic Apps > Add Application > MCP Server
  App name:     cmuir-opensearch
  Backend URL:  http://ping-mcpgw-opensearch-mcp-server/mcp
                (K8s service: ping-mcpgw-opensearch-mcp-server, port 80 → 9900)
  Auth Mode:    Static Token (empty — opensearch-mcp-server is unauthenticated)
  Mesh Cluster: your registered gateway (the one enrolled with the proxy token)

The mcpgw binary will then serve requests at /cmuir-opensearch/mcp.

For OpenSearch to have data: deploy the stack with opensearch.enabled=true (already
set in k8s/aws/deploy.sh when PUBLIC_APP_URL is provided). Or for Docker:
  docker compose --profile mcpgw up -d opensearch opensearch-mcp-server

Starts PKCE against the cmuir-opensearch app's mcpgw path.
Open the returned authUrl in a browser (silent if already signed in).

Lists tools from the OpenSearch MCP server via the cmuir-opensearch Privilege app.

Expect: tools like search_documents, index_document, list_indices — depending on the
opensearch-mcp-server implementation. Privilege policy applies here too.

item.description: Requires cmuir-opensearch registered in Privilege console. See request 6 description.
